notes:
High-level: Verdigris builds an IDE-centric copilot for enterprise dev teams. Primary ask: repo-aware retrieval with deterministic code completions and low-latency streaming inside VS Code. They want embeddings + vector DB to power retrieval, but must keep EU residency for customer code and audit trail.

Technical requirements / preferences: 
- Workload: interactive completions + chat assistant + fuzzy repo search + semantic code navigation.
- Latency: token-first-byte < 50ms ideally for in-editor streaming; end-to-end round-trip for completion < 150ms for short snippets.
- Throughput: peak 600 qps across customers, baseline 120 qps.
- Embeddings: prefer open/quantized embeddings (cost sensitive) with local inference option; want ability to swap embedding model without reindexing (or have reindex tooling).
- Chunking strategy: function/class-level split, ~256-512 token chunks with 20% overlap, language-aware tokenizers for Python/TS/Java.
- Vector DB: lean to self-hosted Milvus or Redis Vector on VPC; explicit requirement to host vectors in EU region.
- Model/versioning: strict pinning for production copilot; automatic fallback to smaller, cheaper models under load with auditable fallback logs.
- Security: SSO (SAML), per-tenant KMS for encryption-at-rest, detailed audit logs (who asked what, which model responded, which candidate context used).
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, recall/precision by prompt set; regression alerts on eval prompts.

POC plan summary: ingest two canonical repos (frontend monorepo ~1.2M LOC, backend services ~0.8M LOC); run embedding + ann indexing in customer's EU VPC. Validate latency in VS Code extension (local dev network) and measure retrieval recall on 3k synthetic queries.

Sales notes / quotes: "We need pinning so customers don't wake up to changed completions overnight." — Head of Product.

Risks / blockers: Legal wants explicit data residency SLA; infra team needs detailed network diagram for private deployment; vector DB ops unknown for their SRE.

Action items: create SOW + infra diagram, share dedicated pricing sheet, schedule 60-min POC kickoff (Liam to own scheduling).
summary: Developer tools co. evaluating Redwood Private/Dedicated for an IDE copilot product that requires EU-resident vector DB, deterministic model pinning, low-latency streaming in VS Code, and strong audit/KMS controls. POC planned to validate embedding pipeline, chunking, and in-editor latency metrics.
